summary: Follow-up to 2026-10-09-session-model-groundwork after PRs #136, #137, #139, #140, #142, #143, and #145 landed: writer-spelled numbers, the D21 native-limit classification, plugin event types in replay, provider usage numbers, Windows-name layout on POSIX (D26), in-memory migration for bake-cli lookup, and the iterative Session payload parser (D27). The development-only bake-session and bake-cli crates are compared with TypeScript through 38 shared case tables (3468 cases) and three runtime captures. A clean checkout of candidate 7698e6d7fba43c0e23cdbf0cd093571e8b99bd1c passed 492 workspace Cargo tests and 4245 Vitest tests (5 skipped) in the 42 TypeScript specs that read those tables. CI for PR #145 tested synthetic merge d552d05a0cd0cc2f1cc5bdcf725fe32f094e7047, which has the candidate's tree c48b9136c93393a4f653090ded220b29eb5ab3cf, and passed the native, runtime, and app-check jobs. One flipped shared-table expectation was rejected by both harnesses. The classification holds 114 limits: 87 unreachable, 4 reachable gaps, and 23 undecided; the migration depth bound (whose fix also closes the two pass-through gaps; D26 accepts the Windows-name gap as an owner exception), the undecided limits, children's own logs, Agent resume, crash recovery, a Windows-host run of 35 of the specs for this candidate, and full preflight are missing. Not scope acceptance.

results.behavior: All 42 TypeScript specs under packages/ that read a conformance/session or conformance/runtime table passed: 4245 Vitest tests passed and 5 skipped (four win32-only lookup cases and the win32-only limit-windows-name plain-log-file case on this POSIX host). Counts describe Vitest tests across 42 files, not table cases.

cargo test --workspace --locked passed 492 tests across 57 test targets (4 doc-test targets ran none). bake-session contributed 158: 70 unit tests and 88 integration tests in 38 binaries, most of which iterate a whole shared table inside one test, so counts describe Cargo tests, not cases. Formatting, clippy, and rustdoc were not run locally for this record.

docs/roadmap/rust-0.4/scope-02/native-limits.json (sha256 in the fixture manifest) classifies 114 native limits against D21: 87 unreachable, 4 reachable gaps (migration-row-json-parser, log-file-windows-name, log-file-migration, cli-migration-limit), and 23 undecided. rust/crates/bake-session/tests/native_limit_classification.rs, which passed 2 tests inside cargo-test, checks the classification against every limit variant and every native-limit expectation in the case tables. The check proves the table is complete and consistent, not that a classification is right.

On PR #145's synthetic merge d552d05a0cd0cc2f1cc5bdcf725fe32f094e7047 (candidate tree), native preflight passed 5 gates on Linux and macOS (rust, rust-pty, rust-conformance, rust-eval, rust-lease) and 4 on Windows with rust-pty skipped (native ConPTY scenarios are not implemented). Counts describe gates.

The rust jobs then ran seven of the 42 conformance specs (lookup, generation-header, stat, list, v2-to-v3 migration, subagent projection and catalog) on each OS: 844 passed and 4 skipped on Linux, 841 and 7 on macOS, 807 and 41 on Windows. Counts describe Vitest tests across those seven files.

The same run's runtime job passed the build, runtime (whole suite, since no merge base was found), and integration gates on Linux at the candidate tree; the earlier record had to cite another PR's runtime job. Counts describe gates.

App checks with --full --skip runtime,native passed 27 gates and skipped 9 on Linux, including typecheck, lint, verify-persistence-catalog, verify-rust-migration-inventory, the ledger verifier, tui-spec, and e2e; whitespace (no merge base), actionlint, and the seven runtime and native gates skipped by flag were the skips. Counts describe gates.

Several tables carry explicit native-limit refusals that the Rust tests require instead of the TypeScript outcome. This checks refuse-rather-than-guess; it is not parity for those cases. Of the 4 reachable gaps, D26 accepts log-file-windows-name as an owner exception to D21, and the other 3 are the migration depth bound and the two pass-through rows that carry it; the 23 undecided limits are not yet shown to be permitted by D21. The groundwork record's fractional-number gap is closed: restore-cases version 3 restores every number spelled as JSON.stringify writes its value, and usage-fraction and context-fraction lost their Rust overrides.

The windows-release job, which builds a release on a Windows host and runs ten runtime specs there, six of them shared-table conformance specs (header, log-scan, source-event-seqs, event-envelope, v3-row, and request-derivation).

missingEvidence.reason: migration-row-json-parser, a reachable gap, keeps the older-generation migrations' 128-level parse bound because their transforms recurse; the stack-safe migration port is in progress and unrecorded here, and no case witnesses the bound.

log-file-migration and cli-migration-limit are reachable gaps only because they pass migration-row-json-parser's depth bound through (native-limits.md, Reachable gaps); they close with the migration depth bound above, and cli-migration-limit also follows the undecided migrated-restore-restore. No separate port is open for them. The fourth reachable gap, log-file-windows-name on a Win32 path platform, is accepted by D26 as an owner exception to D21 and has no follow-up.
23 of the 114 classified limits (64 cases) are undecided: whether a released writer reaches them is not traced.
